newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carlos the Jackal faces December trial in France.
newsitem.headline: Carlos the Jackal faces December trial in France.

text.p: Guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal" will go on trial in Paris on December 12 for the murder of two French counter-intelligence officers in the French capital in 1975, justice sources said on Thursday.
Carlos, in custody in France since August 1994, was tried for the murders in absentia in 1992 and handed a life sentence.
A new trial is required under French law for anyone seized after they have been convicted in their absence.
In the first trial, the Venezuelan-born Carlos, whose real name is Illich Ramirez Sanchez, was convicted of shooting dead two officers of the DST counter-intelligence service.
Raymond Dous and Jean Donatini were shot as they arrived at a flat in Paris's Latin Quarter on June 27, 1975, to question him. Another DST officer, Jean Herranz, was badly wounded but survived.

During questioning by chief anti-terrorism investigator Jean-Louis Bruguiere, Carlos has denied committing the murders but refused to answer questions about the shooting, saying he could not reveal the secrets of his "revolutionary organisation", justice sources said.

The Paris-based Al-Watan al-Arabi magazine quoted Carlos as bragging about the killings in a 1979 interview. But since his arrest, Carlos has denied giving the interview, saying it was planted by an unspecified Arab country's secret service

Carlos is also under investigation in France for a series of other attacks including a 1983 railway station bombing in Marseille which killed two people, the bombing of a high-speed train the same day in which two died, and an explosion on a Paris-Toulouse train in 1982 which killed five people.
France says he killed a total of 83 people in a series of attacks, mostly in Europe and the Middle East.
His boldest guerrilla action was to lead the 1975 kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers attending a conference in Vienna.
